name: Lipoid Proteinosis

ethnicAssociations: Higher prevalence in South African and Turkish populations

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Histopathological Diagnostic Criteria for Lipoid Proteinosis

criteria.description: Early onset hoarseness of voice due to vocal cord infiltration
Presence of hyaline material deposits in skin and mucosa confirmed by biopsy
Characteristic beaded papules along the eyelid margins (moniliform blepharosis)
Calcifications in the medial temporal lobes (amygdala) on imaging

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of early hoarseness plus histopathological confirmation of hyaline deposits in skin or mucosa
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing for ECM1 mutations can support diagnosis but is not mandatory

pathognomonic.symptomName: Beaded papules along eyelid margins (moniliform blepharosis)
Hyaline material deposition in skin and mucosa confirmed by biopsy

common.symptomName: Oral mucosal infiltration with thickened tongue and restricted mobility

occasional.symptomName: Neuropsychiatric symptoms including anxiety and memory impairment
Calcifications in medial temporal lobes on imaging

rare.symptomName: Respiratory distress due to laryngeal infiltration

laboratory: Histopathology showing PAS-positive hyaline deposits in dermis and mucosa
imaging: CT or MRI showing bilateral calcifications in medial temporal lobes (amygdala)
genetic: Mutations in ECM1 gene on chromosome 1q21
other: Laryngoscopy revealing thickened vocal cords with hyaline infiltration

distinguishingFeatures: Amyloid deposits rather than hyaline material

redFlags: Progressive respiratory distress due to laryngeal involvement
references: Urbach W, Wiethe C. Lipoidosis cutis et mucosae. Virchows Arch Pathol Anat. 1929.
Hamada T, et al. Lipoid proteinosis: clinical and molecular aspects. J Dermatol. 2011.
Chan I, et al. ECM1 mutations in lipoid proteinosis. Hum Mutat. 2007.
